paragraphs: Yehudah Hindua, from Cush, which the entry renders Hindaavah in Aramaic. [Rashi gives this gloss in Kiddushin. The checked Targums on Genesis 2:13 retain Cush.] Yoma 81b: himalta from the house of Hinduaei; Rashi explains from Cush. He and his son Rav Shmuel (see there) converted. [Rashi on Yevamot says that Shmuel and his father converted, and Tosafot cite Rabbeinu Tam’s identification of his father as Yehudah Hindua. Kiddushin describes Yehudah as having no heirs.] Bava Batra 74b: he relates. Mar Zutra acquired his property, as the entry reports under Ba Siman, Niddah 49b. [The checked Tosafot there discuss the conversion and heirlessness. The acquisition is described for the enslaved person in Kiddushin.] Mar Zutra was with him before his death and took possession of his slave before he died, as the entry reports: Kiddushin 22b, near the end. [Rashi understands the instruction to remove his shoes as directed at establishing possession at the death. The passage continues on 23a with another version in which the enslaved person was a minor.]
